LESSON: ATHLETICS

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Performing and Displaying
Topic 2.1: Athletics

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Athletics. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How is the jumping skill useful in athletics?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe Long jump and High jump techniques in athletics
2. perform the sail technique in Long jump for skills acquisition
3. perform the scissors technique in High jump for skills acquisition
4. appreciate Long jump and High jump techniques in athletics for enjoyment

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ATHLETICS
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Athletics helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: ATHLETICS
Study Athletics like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe Long jump and High jump techniques in athletics

What this means
In this part you learn to describe Long jump and High jump techniques in athletics. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe Long jump and High jump techniques in athletics.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Athletics” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe Long jump and High jump techniques in athletics. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Perform the sail technique in Long jump for skills acquisition

What this means
In this part you learn to perform the sail technique in Long jump for skills acquisition. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: perform the sail technique in Long jump for skills acquisition.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Athletics in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can perform the sail technique in Long jump for skills acquisition. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Perform the scissors technique in High jump for skills acquisition

What this means
In this part you learn to perform the scissors technique in High jump for skills acquisition. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: perform the scissors technique in High jump for skills acquisition.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can perform the scissors technique in High jump for skills acquisition. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate Long jump and High jump techniques in athletics for enjoyment

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate Long jump and High jump techniques in athletics for enjoyment. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate Long jump and High jump techniques in athletics for enjoyment.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Athletics” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate Long jump and High jump techniques in athletics for enjoyment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Athletics is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Athletics” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe Long jump and High jump techniques in athletics)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Athletics in your own words. (skill: perform the sail technique in Long jump for skills acquisition)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: perform the scissors technique in High jump for skills acquisition)

Example 4: Show how “Athletics” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: appreciate Long jump and High jump techniques in athletics for enjoyment)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Athletics to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe Long jump and High jump techniques in athletics.
3. Practise this skill: perform the sail technique in Long jump for skills acquisition.
4. Practise this skill: perform the scissors technique in High jump for skills acquisition.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Athletics from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Athletics: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Athletics?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How is the jumping skill useful in athletics?
2. Why is it important to maintain a pace in athletics?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Athletics means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe Long jump and High jump techniques in athletics.
5. Be able to: perform the sail technique in Long jump for skills acquisition.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
